chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: Will Heflin, his brother Leon, and taking over the Alabam
summary: Spikes and Will Heflin ran the Alabam around 1930-31 after Mosby closed; Leon Heflin went from furniture and coffins to promoting big bands at Wrigley Field.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What...do you know what years that was?
Yeah, it was about...uh, '30, I guess...'31-- same time we was runnin' the Alabam--Will Heflin and I--around that time.
You and Will Heflin came in...uh, after...
After Mosby closed up.
And Earl Dancer--where did he fit in?

SPIKES - 122
Reel 4
Page 16
He was next door...in the...in the hotel.
In the cabaret in the hotel. Oh, I see.
And we were in the Alabam, which is this side.
Yeah. You know the club.
And so what relation is Will Heflin to Leon Heflin?
Brothers.
I see, because I knew Leon Heflin's name from the Cavalcade of Jazz.

Yeah, well, then, Leon Heflin used to have a big furniture factory here. He was pretty smart boy. He had a great big furniture factory, then after his furniture factory kinda failed, he went into the coffin business--building coffins, and then after that, he ...let's see, what else...then he went into the...uh, promoting jazz. He had all the big bands that come through here. He would have, like, if Duke would come through, and if he had two, three days, he would give him a shot over at the ballpark or somewhere. He would lease the ballpark and...and put him on in percentage or pay him whatever it was but he was a promoter, you see. All the big bands that come through, he got so that his name was so big that used to write him; "Well, we'll be in Los Angeles on the 20th, and we got a coupla days," and he would book 'em somewhere.
So...and the ballpark was Wrigley Field, right?
Yeah, and...Wrigley Field--you know where it was?
Yeah, I remember where it was.

SPIKES - 123
Reel 4
Page 17

At 48th and San Pedro, I think it is. And then he got so that that was his business. He just booked bands. And sometime he'd take 'em up, maybe to Fresno, Bakersfield or somewhere and book 'em and...yeah.
And so Will Heflin, uh, you and he operated the Alabam. What else did he...did he have a background in the entertainment business, too?
Oh, he was just one of them guys that's into everything.
Oh, because I didn't know his name before.

[laughs] He was into everything. Whenever they'd have a big parade downtown and everything, he'd get on Third and Spring or Fifth and Spring or somewhere, and he'd get out there and direct the traffic. Take over! He's one of them kind of guys. He's into everything.
